title: 직장 · 업무
intro: '직장·업무'는 사무실과 함께 일하는 사람 묘사 → 하루 일과 → 기억에 남는 프로젝트·위기 경험 → 입사 초기와 지금(또는 사무실과 재택) 비교 순서로 출제됩니다. 페르소나는 분당의 IT 회사에서 20년째 일하는 소프트웨어 개발팀 리드(팀원 10명)로, 판교 쪽 큰 건물 12층에서 일하고 금요일엔 재택근무를 합니다. '12층 사무실, 오랜 동료 Minho, 5년 전 앱 출시 날 서버 장애' 이야기를 정해 두면 네 문제 모두 같은 스토리로 이어집니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Okay, let me tell you about my office.) → 기본 정보(회사·위치·역할) → 세부(사무실 모습·하루 일과·사람들) → 느낌·이유(팀에 대한 자부심, 일의 보람) → 마무리 문장(Yeah, that's a typical day for me.)
직무 설명은 'software developer, team leader, ten people on my team' 정도의 쉬운 단어로 충분합니다. 어려운 기술 용어는 code review, server, app 정도만 쓰세요.
일과는 9시 출근 → 메시지 확인 → 스탠드업 회의 → 코드 리뷰 → 팀과 점심 → 오후 회의·신입 멘토링 → 내일 할 일 정리 → 7시 퇴근 순서로, First/Then/After that 을 붙여 말하세요.
경험은 '5년 전 쇼핑 앱 출시 날 사용자가 몰려 서버 다운 → 팀 전원 복귀 → 새벽 2시 Minho가 DB 설정 오류 발견 → 3시 복구 → 이후 부하 테스트 필수', 비교는 '20년 전 혼자 코딩·데스크톱·이메일 → 지금 팀 지원·모바일·클라우드·메신저·금요일 재택'으로 준비하세요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you work at a company. Tell me about your office. Where is it, what does it look like, and who do you work with?
questions.ko: 설문에서 회사에 다닌다고 하셨네요. 사무실에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼으며, 누구와 함께 일하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 회사·위치(분당 IT 회사, 판교 쪽 건물 12층, 차로 20분) → 사무실 모습(오픈 공간, 모니터, 회의실, 휴게실) → 함께 일하는 사람(팀원 10명, 동료 Minho) → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
사무실은 엘리베이터에서 내려서 보이는 순서대로 묘사하면 쉬워요
사람 이야기에서 Minho 한 명을 구체적으로 소개하면 다른 질문에도 재활용할 수 있어요

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my office. I work at an IT company in Bundang. My office is on the twelfth floor of a big building in the Pangyo area. It's about twenty minutes from my apartment by car. I'm the leader of a development team, and there are ten people on my team. It's a bright, open place with big windows and long desks. My coworker Minho and I have a lot in common. We have worked together for a long time. Yeah, that's my office.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my office. I work for an IT company in Bundang. Our office is on the twelfth floor of a big glass building. It's located in the Pangyo area, so it's easy to get to. It only takes me about twenty minutes from home by car. It's a bright, open place with long desks, big monitors, and huge windows. There are small meeting rooms on one side and a break room with a coffee machine and snacks on the other. I lead a software development team of ten people. Most of them are in their twenties and thirties, so they keep me young. My coworker Minho and I have a lot in common. We joined the company around the same time, and we both love bad jokes. So yeah, that's where I spend most of my day.
answers.AL: Oh, my office? Let me think. Well, I've been at the same IT company for about twenty years, so the office really feels like a second home. We're on the twelfth floor of a big glass building in the Pangyo area, which is basically Korea's tech valley. It's only about a twenty-minute drive from my apartment, so my commute is pretty easy compared to a lot of people. When you get off the elevator, you walk into a big open space with rows of desks, and almost everyone has two monitors. There are a few glass meeting rooms along one wall, and they're almost always booked. What I like most about the place is that the break room by the window has a great view of the mountains on a clear day. As for the people, I lead a development team of ten. They're mostly young and really smart, and honestly, they teach me new things all the time. My coworker Minho and I have a lot in common. We started at the company around the same time, and we've been through countless late nights and tough launches together, so he's more like family than a coworker. I'd never say that to his face, though. So yeah, that's pretty much my office and the people I work with.

questions.en: Tell me about a typical workday. What do you usually do from the time you get to work until you go home?
questions.ko: 평소 하루 일과에 대해 말해 주세요. 출근해서 퇴근할 때까지 보통 무엇을 하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 출근(9시, 메시지 확인) → 오전(스탠드업 회의, 코드 리뷰) → 점심(팀과) → 오후(회의, 신입 멘토링) → 퇴근(7시, 금요일 재택) → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
First, Then, After that, In the afternoon 같은 시간 표현으로 순서를 잡으세요
팀 리더로서 가장 좋아하는 일(코드 리뷰)을 한 문장 넣으면 느낌·이유가 채워져요

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my typical workday. I get to the office at nine. First, I check my messages. Then, I have a short stand-up meeting with my team. In the morning, I usually review my team's code. I have lunch with my coworkers around noon. In the afternoon, I have a lot of meetings, and I help the new developers. Before I leave, I always write a short to-do list for tomorrow. I usually leave the office at seven. Yeah, that's a typical day for me.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my typical workday. I usually get to the office around nine. First, I check my messages. Then, I have a short stand-up meeting with my team. Everybody shares what they did yesterday and what they're going to do today. After the meeting, I spend a couple of hours reviewing code and giving feedback. Around noon, I have lunch with my team, usually Korean food at a place near our building. The afternoon is full of meetings with other teams. I also spend some time mentoring the new developers, because they have a lot of questions. After that, I usually write a short to-do list for tomorrow to finish my day. I leave around seven and drive home. On Fridays, I work from home. So yeah, that's a typical day as a team leader.
answers.AL: Oh, a typical workday? Let me think. Well, as a team leader, my day is pretty packed, but it has a regular rhythm. I usually get to the office around nine, grab a coffee from the break room, and go through my messages, because there's always something that came in overnight. At nine thirty, we have a quick stand-up meeting, where each person on my team shares what they're working on and whether they're stuck on anything. It only takes fifteen minutes, but it saves us a lot of trouble later. Then I spend most of the morning on code reviews. Honestly, that's the part I enjoy most, because I still get to look at real code. Lunch is usually with my team, and it's a nice chance to chat about something other than work. The afternoon is when things get busy. I've got back-to-back meetings with planners, designers, and other teams, and in between, I try to make time for the junior developers who need help. After that, I usually write a short to-do list for tomorrow to finish my day. I head home around seven, and on the drive, I listen to some nineties ballads to switch off. So yeah, that's pretty much what my day looks like.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at work, such as a big project or a tight deadline. What happened, and why do you remember it so well?
questions.ko: 직장에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험, 예를 들어 큰 프로젝트나 촉박한 마감에 대해 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 왜 그렇게 잘 기억나나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 배경(5년 전, 1년 동안 만든 쇼핑 앱) → 사건(출시 10분 만에 사용자 폭주, 서버 다운) → 해결(팀 전원 복귀, 새벽 2시 Minho가 원인 발견, 3시 복구) → 교훈·느낌 → 'So yeah, that's ~' 마무리
과거 시제로 일관되게! Something unexpected happened when ~ 으로 위기를 시작하세요
숫자(8시 출시, 10분 만에, 새벽 3시)를 넣으면 이야기가 구체적이고 생생해져요

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about a memorable experience at work. About five years ago, my team made a new shopping app. Something unexpected happened when we launched our new app. Too many people used it at once, and the server went down. We were really nervous. My whole team stayed at the office until three in the morning. Finally, Minho found the problem, and we fixed it. Yeah, that's a night I'll never forget.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about a memorable experience at work. About five years ago, my team worked on a new shopping app for almost a year. Something unexpected happened when we launched our new app. We started the service at eight in the evening, and in just ten minutes, way more people logged in than we expected. The server slowed down and then completely crashed. My phone started ringing nonstop, and my boss was really worried. I called my whole team back to the office, and we checked everything together. Luckily, Minho found the problem in the database settings around two in the morning. We fixed it, and the app was back up by three. I'll never forget that night because the whole team worked together until three in the morning. Since then, we always test our systems carefully before a launch. So yeah, that's my most memorable work experience.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable experience at work? Let me think. Well, after twenty years, there are plenty of stories, but one night really stands out. About five years ago, my team spent almost a year building a new shopping app for our company. Launch day finally came, and we were all excited. We opened the service at eight in the evening, and for the first ten minutes, everything looked perfect. Then, out of nowhere, the number of users shot way past what we'd planned for, and the server just crashed. My heart sank. Messages were flooding in, and my boss kept calling me every five minutes. Some of my team had already gone home, but when I asked for help, every single person came back to the office without complaining. We ordered pizza, split up the work, and checked the system piece by piece. Around two in the morning, Minho shouted, 'Found it!' It turned out to be one wrong setting in the database. We fixed it, ran some tests, and by three, the app was running smoothly again. I'll never forget that night because I've never felt so proud of my team. Since then, I always make sure to run load tests before a launch. So yeah, that was a stressful night, but it brought us closer together.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you how my work has changed. I started my job about twenty years ago. I used to write code alone at my desk, but now I spend most of my time helping my team. We also used a lot of email, but now we use chat apps and video calls. These days, I work from home on Fridays. I like a mix of office work and working from home. Yeah, that's how my work has changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about how my work has changed. When I first started about twenty years ago, I was a junior developer. I used to write code alone at my desk, but now I spend most of my time helping my team. Compared to twenty years ago, technology is much more advanced now. Back then, we made software for desktop computers, and there were no smartphones. Now almost everything we build is a mobile app or runs in the cloud. The way we work together has also changed. We used to send long emails and stay late at the office, but now we use chat apps and video calls. I even work from home every Friday. Honestly, I like both. At the office, it's easier to solve problems face to face, but at home, I can focus without interruptions. All things considered, I think a mix of office work and working from home is the best. So yeah, that's how my work has changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a big question for me. Let me think. Well, I've been doing this job for about twenty years, so pretty much everything has changed. When I started, I was a junior developer fresh out of college with a degree in electronic engineering. I used to write code alone at my desk all day, but now I spend most of my time helping my team, reviewing their code, and sitting in meetings. Compared to my first year, technology is much more advanced. Back then, we built programs for desktop computers, nobody had a smartphone, and we tested everything by hand. Now we build mobile apps that run in the cloud, and we even use AI tools that suggest code as we type, which still amazes me. How we work together has changed, too. Twenty years ago, if you wanted to talk to someone, you either walked over to their desk or sent a long email. Now everything happens in team chat and video calls, and working from home is completely normal. I work from home every Friday, and I can focus much better without people tapping me on the shoulder. Still, some things are just easier face to face, like brainstorming or helping a new hire who's struggling. All things considered, I think a mix of office work and working from home is the best. So yeah, that's how my work has changed over twenty years.

parts.ko: 그 후에는 보통 신입 개발자들을 멘토링하고 내일 할 일 목록을 짧게 적으며 하루를 마무리해요.

parts.en: I'll never forget the night we launched our new shopping app about five years ago because the server crashed just ten minutes after we opened the service.
parts.ko: 서비스를 연 지 겨우 10분 만에 서버가 다운돼서, 5년 전쯤 새 쇼핑 앱을 출시한 그날 밤을 절대 잊지 못할 거예요.

parts.en: I was so nervous that my heart sank, and my boss kept calling me every five minutes.
parts.ko: 너무 긴장해서 가슴이 철렁했고, 상사는 5분마다 계속 전화를 했어요.

parts.en: I didn't know what to do, so I called my whole team back to the office to check everything together.
parts.ko: 어떻게 해야 할지 몰라서 팀원 전체를 사무실로 다시 불러 모든 걸 함께 점검했어요.

parts.en: Since then, I always make sure to test our servers with far more users than we expect before any big launch.
parts.ko: 그 이후로는 큰 출시를 앞두고 항상 예상보다 훨씬 많은 사용자로 서버를 테스트해요.
